units.name: Biology (Genetics & Evolution)
objectives: Be able to define the following terms: gene, allele, dominant, recessive, genotype, phenotype, homozygous, heterozygous.
Be able to use a Punnett square to determine the genotype and phenotype of traits.
Understand that an individual can be a carrier of a recessive disease, and that a sufferer must be homozygous recessive for it.
Be able to complete a Punnett square to predict the probability of a recessive disease.
Know that a mutation is a permanent change to a DNA sequence, and that it can change the proteins produced by transcription and translation.
Know that a mutation can change an organism's genotype, and therefore its phenotype.
Recognise that pedigree charts are used to trace a family history of showing or carrying certain traits, and to work out how likely offspring are to show or carry them.
Be able to interpret pedigree charts for autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive traits.
Be able to identify carriers in a pedigree chart.
Understand the difference between a genetic and an acquired trait.
Be able to explain how a new variant of a genetic trait can arise in a population.
Define evolution and explain why variation is needed for evolution to occur.
Define natural selection and give examples of selection pressures and how they may affect a population.
Be able to explain how species evolve adaptations through natural selection.
Be able to tell the difference between behavioural, physiological and structural adaptations.
Be able to describe the main types of evidence that support the theory of evolution.
Define species and be able to summarise the process of speciation.
